Alex S.: hey @emily thanks for the report — can you grab a HAR + console export for the SSO redirect that results in a 0-byte/blank page? Need request IDs and a curl repro so eng can trace the handoff to the IdP. Steps below.

Emily (customer): sure — do you want the full session including cookies? there are emails in the payload.

Alex S.: good question. yes, include cookies in the HAR export so we can see the redirect chain, but please redact tokens and PII before uploading. exact steps: 1) reproduce in an Incognito window (disable extensions) so we get a clean trace. 2) Open DevTools -> Network: check 'Preserve log' and 'Disable cache'. 3) Reproduce the flow: click Sign in -> follow redirects until you hit the blank page. 4) Right-click the network table -> 'Save all as HAR with content' (Chrome) and attach. 5) Console: switch to Console panel -> right-click -> 'Save as...' or copy the console output and save to a .txt.

Alex S.: curl repro (helps us reproduce redirect chain server-side):
```
# follow redirects, write cookies, dump headers
curl -v -L -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt -D response_headers.txt -o /dev/null 'https://app.redwood.ai/login?redirect=/app'

# after authenticating in the browser, hit the app API using cookie jar
curl -v -H 'Accept: application/json' -b cookies.txt 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/session'
```

Alex S.: in response_headers.txt look for X-Request-Id or X-Request-ID (paste that into the support ticket). also include the URL you clicked, your approximate local time, browser/version (Chrome 117, MacOS 13.4, etc).

Alex S.: anonymization tips before upload: open the HAR in a text editor and replace any Authorization headers or long bearer tokens with "<REDACTED>", and replace any user emails in request bodies with "[email redacted]". you can still keep cookies in the HAR so we can see session cookies, but redact their values if you prefer and paste them into a separate file.

support-bot: Automated: linked ticket #45672 to this thread.

Priya V.: I can take the backend side once you post the request-id and timestamp. If you can also include IdP timestamp from your side that helps (Auth0/Okta/GSuite logs).

Emily (customer): uploading now — HAR is ~8.2MB. I replaced Authorization with <REDACTED> and emails with [email redacted]. attaching response_headers.txt and the curl -v output. request id I see in the headers = 7f9b2c1a-4d8e-4a3b-b2d1-12f9e6c3a701

Jordan K.: quick extras — if this only happens on Chrome, try Firefox and also repro with network throttling off. also temporarily disable any SSO-helper extension (eg. Okta browser plugin). clock skew on client machine can cause redirect to fail during token exchange, check system time.

Priya V.: got the request-id, pulling logs for 2024-05-14T14:32:00Z -> 2024-05-14T14:33:00Z now. I'll post findings here. :thumbsup:

Alex S.: thanks @Emily — once Priya confirms, we'll ask IdP team for the matching auth logs. appreciate the quick repro. :pray:
